promises.raised_by: birju reading 89,400 against his own house in the open yard
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: where the figure came from and whether it can be made to move the other way
promises.how_paid: the chain is traced entry by entry from the 1974 advance through the 1991 division and the 2009 consolidation, and the reason it only ever grows is established: there is no credit column.

promises.raised_by: phulwa's 2009 thumbprint on the line above the figure
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: what she put her thumb on and who let her
promises.how_paid: phulwa states that birju himself read the paper to her at twelve and told her it was a receipt; the page is produced and cancelled by the officer's own hand in ep14.

promises.raised_by: sanichari's 63,200 read aloud
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: whether anything in that book can ever be corrected
promises.how_paid: a triple-entered 3,000 fine is exposed in front of the government clerk and 6,000 struck off aloud, with the reason written in words.

promises.raised_by: chameli's father calling off the marriage in the ration queue
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: the same man taking it back in the same place
promises.how_paid: in the same queue at the crossing, in front of the same people, he says 'Baisakh, then. Before the firing.'

promises.raised_by: the torn page numbered 411
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: the earlier book, and what is on its first page
promises.how_paid: the almirah key; nine volumes; volume one, 1974, entry one — 5,000 rupees, purpose marriage, birju's grandfather's thumbprint.

promises.raised_by: tirath's claim of eleven years and four months, four of them unpaid
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: tirath being paid the four months
promises.how_paid: 19,200 rupees paid in the office on the Monday, with the door open, in front of men who had been stepping over his legs at the crossing.

promises.raised_by: lakhan's terms — one season where the number moves the right way, and cash in the open at the crossing
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: lakhan paid in cash, in public
promises.how_paid: dhaniram counts 8,400 rupees into lakhan's hand at the crossing in front of twenty people; birju counts it aloud because lakhan will not.

promises.raised_by: birju asking dhaniram which column a payment goes in
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: the answer dhaniram refused to give
promises.how_paid: tirath: never once in eleven years and four months. Then the page itself: five columns, none of them a credit column.

promises.raised_by: dhaniram naming the green tin behind phulwa's stove
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: what he intends to do with her papers
promises.how_paid: the ration card is gone from the tin; devlal took it at the shop in Poos and used it to build the transfer of her household to Kaimur.

promises.raised_by: birju's own name entered on page twelve as a debtor for 4,000 in his own certified hand
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: what else he has signed without reading
promises.how_paid: the forty-one blank certification slips he signed on the day he took the chair; one of them is the transfer of his mother. Both the 4,000 and the transfer are cancelled by the certificates in ep14.

promises.raised_by: maqsood's rule that the number travels with the household
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: whether anyone can ever get out from under it
promises.how_paid: a release certificate cancels rather than reduces, so a transferred debt that no longer exists cannot be transferred; the four households come back from Kaimur on the Thursday.

promises.raised_by: sanichari asking birju to check her drowned son's number
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: ramnath's line closed
promises.how_paid: 22,400 struck in the open yard with eight other deceased lines, reason written in words, countersigned by the licensee.

promises.raised_by: rajni: 'either useful to you or a problem for you, and I am not the one who decides which'
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: which it turns out to be
promises.how_paid: both. The correction on her file makes the book the finest in the block and therefore unassailable — and it also names birju as the person who maintains it, which is what makes him unremovable from the inquiry.

promises.raised_by: devlal striking lakhan with the scale pan while birju stayed in the doorway
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: devlal answering for it, and birju answering for the doorway
promises.how_paid: devlal is named in the officer's finding alongside his father and his matter is in court; the 2,000 'insolence' fine is repaid in cash at the crossing; birju's failure is stated plainly by the narrator and never excused.

promises.raised_by: the hundred fine slips ruled and headed in birju's hand
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: his own neatness turned around
promises.how_paid: the same hand rules the credit column on the last page of volume nine, and the same headed, initialled, checkable book becomes the evidence that ends the site.

promises.raised_by: dhaniram asking for one figure divisible by three
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: the total, and what it does when it exists
promises.how_paid: 11,40,000 against forty-one households, produced on oath — and the other side of it, 1,09,46,000 short at the printed rate, produced in the same breath.

promises.raised_by: entry one, 1974, 5,000 rupees, purpose marriage, birju's grandfather
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: that account closed
promises.how_paid: dhaniram signs a receipt for 1,62,000 rupees in settlement of the account opened in 1974, and it is read back to him aloud, twice.

promises.raised_by: sudama's mother's 1,100 rupees written in pencil in a trimmed margin
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: money that reached the debt at last
promises.how_paid: her line goes to zero with the rest under the certificate; sudama makes three people at the crossing say his name and then goes back to Punjab anyway.

promises.raised_by: sudama's 39,600 in a belt and the 16,000 sent from Punjab
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: whether that money was simply lost
promises.how_paid: it was never entered against the debt and never could be — the shop's own receipts are produced at the inquiry as part of what the site can prove it received, and they reduce the site's credit side by exactly that much.

promises.raised_by: birju refusing to sign hemwati's complaint and naming the appointment letter as the reason
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: him signing it
promises.how_paid: hemwati gets her thirty-second signature at four o'clock on the bonnet of the jeep, after the finding, having already got what she actually needed: the accounts produced on oath.

promises.raised_by: line nine in handwriting that is not birju's
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: who supplied his mother's figure
promises.how_paid: lakhan walked nine kilometres and recited sixty-one households from memory, from the one afternoon his brother read them aloud, and refused to put his thumb on anything.

promises.raised_by: four households on a truck to Kaimur under birju's genuine signature
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: phulwa back, and the signature answered for
promises.how_paid: the certificate cancels the debt, so there is nothing left to transfer; maqsood drives them back on the Thursday and does not charge for the diesel.

promises.raised_by: sixty-two release certificates unsigned in a block office almirah for four months
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: them issued
promises.how_paid: rajni brings all sixty-two to teghra more along with sixty-one new ones and stamps them in the yard; her pending count is zero and she asks for it to be noted.

promises.raised_by: the inquiry fixed for the eleventh at eleven o'clock, the officer does not wait
promises.listener_is_waiting_for: what the book says on the day
promises.how_paid: it says both sides. The finding is recorded, the certificates issue, and the government's permanent figure is the one birju ruled at three in the morning on the eighth.

narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.line: 'That is the point of doing it in the open. Remember that.'
narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.how: the same yard, the same four hundred people, the accounts read aloud again — the openness that was the humiliation is the instrument of the reversal.

narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.line: 'He decided not to speak. Write that down somewhere, because in nine weeks he will not be able to remember making the decision.'
narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.how: the forty-one blank slips: the same reflex, at scale, with his mother on one of them.

narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.line: 'It is worth saying plainly, because it will not happen again for a long time.'
narrator_debts_left_open_deliberately.how: four episodes later, and the second time costs nine dead men being described out loud as bad arithmetic.

unwitnessed_canon.what: the trimmed margin carrying the only written record of a payment
unwitnessed_canon.why_left_open: no character in the story ever learns it happened, and nothing in the season depends on their learning it.

unwitnessed_canon.what: the blank certification slip being filled in as a transfer
unwitnessed_canon.why_left_open: the act itself is never witnessed; only its output is ever seen.
